 20. In Title Appeal No. 54 of 186? judgment delivered on 22.03.1862 by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge who after taking into consideration of the question in disputes affirmed the decision of the learned Munsif in respect of Baridari rights. Defendant preferred appeal against the decision of the learned Munsif Moulavi Nasiruddin Nyder, Munsif of Parcoal dated 10.12.1861, learned Sub-Ordinate Judge held as: 

 Explanation-when more than fifty per cent of the net available income of a waqf is exclusively applied for religious and charitable purposes, such a waqf shall be deemed to be a public waqf within the meaning of clause (e) of sub-section (I) of section 85 of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 (EB Act XXIII of 1949)and shall be deemed to be a trust for public purposes of a charitable or religious nature within the meaning of section 92 of the Code of Civil procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908) and section 14 of the Religious Endowments Act, 1863 (Act XX of 1863); 

 In the case of waqf, as per explanation, before declaring the shrine or mazarmasjid or property as waqf, authority must have satisfied about the condition as given under note explanation. Mahamedan law by D.F. Mulla deals matter of waqf As per section 174 of the aforesaid Act, Waqf means permanent dedication by a person professing Mussalman faith of any property for any purpose recognized by the Mussalman law as religious, pious or charitable. Section 175 and 177 of the said Act. for purpose of which a waqf may be created must be one recognizing by the Mahamedan law as "religious, pious or charitable". As per section 178 of the said law, objects of waqf have been mentioned and as per law there are 17 objects of waqf. These laws generally applied for waqf made by a person either orally or by deed. Section 186 of the said law speaks how a wadf can be completed and section 188 of the said law fixed for immemorial user.
